Lines.Text: BANG—!!
The rusty rooftop door screamed open.
P stepped onto the pitch-black roof, dragging in breaths like a man being strangled.
The vicious midnight wind slashed at his cheeks, but his bloodshot eyes wandered through the dark, unable to focus.
He stumbled, caught the railing, and retched like an animal.
(Help us... P... Please save us...)
A piercing whine filled his ears. The girls' cries from the basement practice room slammed through his mind.
Their desperate grip on his crumpled trousers. The heat of the tears dripping onto his worn shoes.
Every sensation remained horribly vivid, tightening around his throat.
Then something in their sobbing began to warp.
Over Jiwoo's young voice, over Ria's trembling pleas... someone else's voice tangled around them like a spider's web.
(Producer... What do we do now...? Please help us...)
Three years ago. The same girl had clung to his trousers and sobbed when the company's cruelty brought her down. It was her voice.
CREEEAK—
Behind him, something stepped onto the old metal railing.
The air froze. The sharp scent of frost and the metallic tang of blood stung his nose.
P stopped breathing and slowly turned.
In darkness beyond the reach of the city lights, a young girl balanced precariously on the edge of the roof.
Blanched cheeks. Empty, ash-gray eyes.
The apparition of the first idol he had produced—the girl who had taken her own life three years ago.
(reaching out with a violently trembling hand) N-no... Don't... Get down from there...! It was me. It was all my fault...!
The apparition swayed as though the wind might shatter her at any moment. She gave him a numb, sorrowful smile.
It wasn't your fault.
I just finally understood... how easily this huge world can chew up someone like me and swallow her whole.
WHOOSH—
With those chilling words, the girl leaned back into empty air.
NO!!!
P screamed and lunged for the railing, reaching out into the void.
His fingers closed on nothing but cold winter air.
The image of her plummeting toward the distant ground burned itself into his eyes.
Poof—
Just before she struck the ground, her falling body crumbled like a broken wing into tens of thousands of white snowflakes.
The silver flakes rose on the wind, scattering across the night sky in defiance of gravity.
So... are you going to run away again?
A rustling whisper mixed into the wind. P flinched and turned.
P whipped his head around. The drifting snow spiraled toward another corner of the railing and wove itself back into the pale girl's shape.
She threw herself into the air again.
Her body broke into snow, and the swirling flakes formed another girl behind his back.
An endless cycle of falling and scattering, terrible and strange.
The girl P had failed to save became a winter apparition, falling before his eyes over and over.
(rolling on the icy roof, clamping his hands over his ears) AAAAAH!! Stop... Please, make it stop...!!
(writhing on the cold rooftop, hands clamped over both ears, screaming) It was the hell P had lived through every night for three years.
(Look the other way. Just like last time.)
Executive Kim's voice wormed its way into his head.
Curled on the ground, P stared at his shaking hands.
Four hundred eighty million won. And the towering monster called S-Tier. He couldn't win this fight.
If he failed again, this time he would lose everything he owned—even his soul—and end up in the street.
Don't throw yourself at a wall you can't break. Bow your head. Find a way to save yourself.
He tried to convince himself that this was what adults called reason. That this was being rational.
Once again, he was reaching for the door marked compromise.
Then it happened.
The apparition stopped. No more falling. No more snow.
The toes of a pair of worn sneakers came to rest before him.
Still curled up and trembling, P slowly raised his head. The girl made of snow looked quietly down at him.

Her eyes were no longer the empty eyes of her final moments. They were clear again, as they had been when she first received one of his songs and beamed as though being allowed onto a stage meant the whole world was hers.
(laying her snow-cold hand over his trembling one) Producer. Haven't you hidden behind being a reasonable adult enough? Wasn't losing me enough?
I didn't die because you thought that wall was too big to break. I died because you were afraid of losing, and you gave up on me.
I died because you got scared first and gave up on me.
Her voice was colder than the winter wind, yet held a strange warmth.
One by one, white snowflakes melted on their joined hands.
Will you leave those girls down there somewhere cold forever, too?
You know what you have to do. This time, the right thing is to protect them. Stay.
The realization struck P like a hammer blow, passing through his whole body.
He had always believed that bowing to S-Tier was the sensible choice.
But she was right. He had mistaken cowardice for reason and called his own refusal to act rational.
At last, the guilt and compromise that had strangled him for three years snapped.
His hands, shaking uncontrollably with fear, went still as if by a miracle.
His hunched shoulders slowly straightened. An incredulous, startlingly clear laugh escaped his split lips.
(slowly getting to his feet, looking into the night with clear eyes) Yeah... I finally get it.
Playing by their rotten rules doesn't make me smart. Putting everything I have on the line to protect those girls... That's the road I should have taken.
He turned with resolve in his eyes. The apparition smiled, radiant with relief.
Then she dissolved into countless shining snowflakes, drifting softly through the winter night.
Only the faintest trace of her warmth remained on his calloused fingertips.
(clenching his fist, murmuring to the scattered snow) They won't take them from me this time.
Even if it costs me every last scrap of flesh, every bone, every won I have... I'll put those girls on the highest stage in the world. I'll make sure they succeed.
The false reason money had taught him burned away. In the dark winter night, his eyes shone cold and clear: at last, he understood what it meant to choose.
P roughly brushed the dirt from his jacket.
The hesitation of a man trapped in the past was gone from his stride. So was the fear that had kept him watching from the sidelines.
For the five girls he had to protect, and for the path he had finally chosen, he walked toward the top-floor boardroom—the heart of the empire.
